A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA memorization study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated and newly added content to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original centralized and federated fine-tuning experiments, medical benchmark accuracy, memorization measurements, privacy-method analyses and secure-aggregation timings.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments on legal and financial datasets, a 70B model, semantic similarity and lower document duplication.

M1.justification: The underlying LoRA and FedAvg procedures remain unchanged, as do the investigated combinations with Goldfish loss, NEFTune, clipping, Gaussian noise and secure aggregation. The additional models, datasets and memorization metric expand evaluation rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates medical QA and injected i2b2 records. v3 Appendix C adds centralized fine-tuning on Multi-LexSum legal summarization and ConvFinQA financial conversational QA, substantially extending the represented domains and tasks while retaining medical coverage.

E2.justification: The round-by-round comparison is narrowed: v1 Figure 8 includes centralized full-fine-tuning and centralized LoRA reference comparators, whereas v3 Figure 4 includes only the two federated methods. Centralized comparisons remain elsewhere. Other comparator sets are retained, and the new domain experiments reuse full fine-tuning versus LoRA.

E3.justification: v3 introduces evaluations with Llama 3.1 70B Instruct, adds rescaled BERTScore using DeBERTa-xlarge-MNLI, and tests threefold duplication alongside the retained duplication settings. These materially extend model configurations and measurement protocols. The original medical splits, five federated rounds, prompting scheme and core hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a targeted threefold-duplication sensitivity check. The existing rank, training-step, Goldfish, NEFTune, clipping and Gaussian-noise analyses largely retain their evidence. Conversely, v1 Figure 8's worst-case 500-token per-round trajectories are omitted from the reduced grid in v3 Figure 4.

E5.justification: Both versions report medical downstream accuracy averaged over three seeds. v3 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests, memorization uncertainty estimates or explicitly increased run counts; the additional tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v3 Tables 4–6 add substantial results for new domains, model scale and metrics. For example, legal-domain 70B BLEU is 0.55 for full fine-tuning versus 0.17 for LoRA; finance gives 0.55 versus 0.50. These are new comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores. Most matched earlier tables retain their values. Table 6 also contains an exception to its caption: nonduplicated medical 3B BERTScore is 0.12 for LoRA versus 0.11 for full fine-tuning.

T1.justification: The federated objective, extractable-memorization definition and delta-compression relationship are retained. The expanded theoretical discussion summarizes cited results and proposes explanations involving regularization and DP-SGD, without developing new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions expand the claimed applicability from medical experiments with smaller models to medicine, law and finance and models up to 70B. Novelty is refocused from previously unquantified LoRA memorization effects generally to their empirical study in federated learning. The central claim of up to tenfold reduction with little performance cost remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations involving architecture differences, client-specific learning rates, regularization and connections to DP-SGD. It discusses early-round exceptions and the implications of selecting the final federated round. The conclusion newly emphasizes limited applicability to small cross-silo settings and residual memorization, while v1's explicit future-work qualifications about pretraining and alternative memorization definitions are dropped.

D1.justification: v3 adds GPU-hour budgets, an eight-GPU setup for the 70B model, BERTScore implementation details, and dataset/model source and licensing information. The repository pointer changes. Most existing hyperparameter disclosures remain, although v1's explicit dataset-size weighting formula for clients is no longer stated.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against centralized LoRA memorization studies by Hou et al. and Wang and Li, federated PEFT research, and recent privacy literature. Section 5 additionally connects the findings to LoRA regularization, expressivity and DP-SGD research. These additions redefine the research gap rather than merely update bibliography metadata.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten, related work and preliminaries are combined, and methodology is separated from results. Federated results now precede centralized comparisons. Dataset descriptions and accuracy discussion move into appendices, while rank analysis moves into the main text and theoretical discussion is expanded and redistributed.

P2.justification: The memorization bar charts change from two-row grids to horizontal six-panel layouts. The round-by-round grid is reduced and redrawn; accuracy figures move together into Appendix B, while the illustrative memorization plot and rank table move into the main text. Three new result tables, revised captions and publication-format typography substantially alter presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful additional evidence beyond v1's medical setting, clearer research positioning, explicit cross-silo limitations and better resource documentation. These improve the paper's support and interpretability. The gains are limited because Appendix C's extensions are centralized and lack corresponding downstream-utility results, leaving the broader federated privacy–utility claims incompletely supported. Its blanket claim that all metrics decrease also conflicts with Table 6's BERTScore exception.
